title: Problem Set 7 — Related Rates
subject: Calculus
sourceText:
Calculus — Problem Set 7: Related Rates

Useful fact: the volume of a sphere is V = (4/3)πr³.

Worked excerpt:
   Air enters a spherical balloon at a rate of dV/dt = 100 cm³/s.
   Differentiating both sides with respect to t gives
       dV/dt = 4πr² · dr/dt.
   Solve for dr/dt at the instant r = 5 cm.

Problems:
1) A snowball melts so that its surface area shrinks at a constant rate.
   Its radius satisfies S = 4πr². Find dS/dt in terms of r and dr/dt.
2) A ladder slides away from a wall. Let x be the distance from the wall
   and y the height on the wall, with x² + y² = 25.
   Differentiate the whole equation with respect to t.

Reminder: keep every rate labeled — dV/dt, dr/dt, dx/dt — and say which
instant each number belongs to.

marks.label: reading d/dt
marks.why: The excerpt opens with dV/dt = 100 cm³/s as if the notation reads itself. It doesn't have to stay opaque — one naming pass and it does.

steps.text: Read d/dt as one indivisible symbol: 'the rate of change of … with respect to time.'
So dV/dt names a single object — how fast V changes per second. It is not V divided by anything.
Units confirm the reading: V is in cm³, t in s, so dV/dt wears cm³/s. A rate, exactly as promised.
In the excerpt, dV/dt = 100 cm³/s is a GIVEN rate. The question hunts a different one: dr/dt.

check.prompt: Apply the move: in the statement dV/dt = 100 cm³/s, what does dV/dt name? Answer in words.

marks.label: the chain rule as a rates converter
marks.why: The excerpt's line dV/dt = 4πr² · dr/dt contains a silent step: the chain rule inserting dr/dt. Rebuilding that step makes the line derivable instead of magical.

steps.text: When a quantity depends on t only through another variable, differentiating pulls in an extra factor.
The rule: d/dt[ f(g(t)) ] = f′(g(t)) · g′(t). In words: outside derivative × inside derivative.
Balloon version: V depends on r, and r depends on t, so dV/dt = (dV/dr) · (dr/dt).
Compute the outside piece: dV/dr from V = (4/3)πr³ is 4πr².
Multiply by the inside piece dr/dt and the excerpt's line is rebuilt: dV/dt = 4πr² · dr/dt. The trailing dr/dt is not decoration — it is the chain rule's fee.

check.prompt: Apply the move: x = y³ and y = 1 + t². Write dx/dt in terms of y and t.

nextLine.setup: Problem 1: a spherical balloon holds V = (4/3)πr³ with air entering at dV/dt = 100 cm³/s. The excerpt jumps straight to the differentiated line — but you write YOUR next line: differentiate both sides with respect to t.

expect.hint: Differentiate the right side as a chain: the derivative of r³ brings down 3r² and a fee of dr/dt; (4/3)π · 3 simplifies to 4π. So the line is dV/dt = 4πr² · dr/dt.
